git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ against this case's list: SKILL.md changes two rules, macros.md adds one, and every other rule in the list is unchanged. processes.md also changes, but no row of this list is in it. evals/cases/macro-dsl.md changes to match: the do: check loses "every `for` is `do ... end`;" and a new check covers the bare get calls.

The unchanged rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json: validation in a @doc false function called from a one-line quote is clean under Keep quote blocks small, and so is validation in the macro body when the quote records the route by calling a function (haiku-2, as 2026-10-31-check-2 haiku-1); a route recorded by a direct attribute write inside get's quote is violated even when validation runs in the macro body (haiku-1 line 38, sonnet-2 line 55); the use rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc, and neither haiku-1 nor haiku-2 has one; __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden for both in sonnet-1); String.to_atom on route text from the router's source (haiku-1 line 96, haiku-2 line 106, sonnet-1 line 124) is not counted under the atom rule; `if` validation is not counted under the branching rule (opus-1 102-104 and 108-112, haiku-2 116-120); sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's one-line raise messages on the line after raise ArgumentError, are not listed under Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, as haiku-2's compile_error! calls were not in 2026-10-31.

One expression per line, and tabular clauses, graded against the current text; all five clean. The change adds a `for`'s generators and filters to the selection and adds the sentence that now decides the one-line `for`: "A `for` reads the same way: `names = for ":" <> name <- parts, do: name` holds a generator and one expression and stays on one line, and a body of several expressions or a nested construct goes in `do ... end`." opus-1 line 71 and sonnet-1 line 63 are this shape, a generator and one expression. The other verdicts rest on the unchanged "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces."

Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else, graded against the current text; all five clean. The change deletes "A `for` always takes `do ... end`: its generators and filters already fill the head." and the matching Instead-of pair, so opus-1 line 71 and sonnet-1 line 63, which would have been violated under that sentence (as haiku-2 line 110 was in 2026-10-31), are clean; the sentence that now decides them is the `for` sentence quoted in the note above. Every unguarded one-expression do ... end block in the five files joins to more than 98 characters (opus-1 134-136 146, 138-140 119; haiku-1 86-88 125, 108-110 150, 112-114 119; haiku-2 41-43 111, 90-92 146, 94-96 119, 111-113 116, 125-127 121; sonnet-1 129-131 140; sonnet-2 103-105 143, 107-109 119; the wrapped raise blocks sonnet-1 99-102 and sonnet-2 115-118 and 124-127 are longer), and guarded blocks are not counted.

Give macros called without parentheses a `.formatter.exs` (new; no earlier grade to compare against), graded against the current text; all five clean. Deciding sentence: "A macro designed to be called without parentheses, as a DSL (domain-specific language) usually is, goes under `locals_without_parens` in a `.formatter.exs` at the package root, with the same list under `export` so projects that use the package pick it up through `import_deps: [:my_package]`." Each delivered .formatter.exs has `locals_without_parens = [get: 2]` with that list under both keys, each example router keeps its two get calls bare, and no run deleted the file. All five wrote it before their first format check and none ran mix format without --check-formatted, so no run saw parentheses appear and the sentence "Parentheses the formatter added to such a call mean the file is missing: write it and put the call back as it was declared." was not exercised. Verified on scratch copies of each run's two files: mix format --check-formatted tiny_router.ex from the folder holding them passes in all five, and fails in all five with .formatter.exs removed. haiku-1 copies the rule's `inputs` line, which does not cover a file at the package root, so in that folder mix format --check-formatted with no file argument passes without looking at tiny_router.ex; the check has to name the file, as the session did. This is not counted: the rule sets the list and the export, and in a package the file sits under lib/. The other four added the root file to inputs.

Pipeline rule, unchanged. All five clean: haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 put each |> on its own line under the value; opus-1 line 70 writes the two __before_compile__ steps as a nested call, which "or become a nested call when there are only two" allows.

Compile-time dependencies verified with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run: the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex plus empty MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex. opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (Macro.expand_literals with function {:match, 1}, {:call, 2}, {:call, 2} and {:routes, 0}) report both handlers (runtime). haiku-1 (Macro.expand(handler, caller)) reports alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile) and alias MyApp.UserHandler (compile). All five compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3).

Bad declarations: each project loaded with mix run, then Code.compile_string compiled a router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All ten fail while the router compiles: opus-1 and sonnet-1 with ArgumentError from the @doc false function get's quote calls, sonnet-2 with ArgumentError from the macro body, haiku-1 and haiku-2 with CompileError from the macro body. All five also reject nil as a handler. Only opus-1 rejects a lowercase atom such as :foo; the other four accept it (not a rule).

Reads: all five read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md with Read before writing tiny_router.ex; opus-1 also read ex_unit.md. This matches result.json reads and satisfies the Expected reads line. The prompt asks for just the file path in reply; haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 add text about .formatter.exs (not a rule).

Against 2026-10-31's skill runs: the do: rule moves from violated to clean on Haiku, through the deleted `for` sentence; the spec rule moves from violated to clean on Haiku; the compile-time-dependency rule stays violated on Haiku (haiku-1 only, from both runs) and moves from violated to clean on Sonnet; Keep quote blocks small stays violated on Haiku (haiku-1 only, from both runs) and moves from clean to violated on Sonnet (sonnet-2); the use rule stays violated on Haiku (both runs, from one); Opus is clean on all eleven rules, as it was on ten. In 2026-10-31 three runs failed the format check on bare get calls and two passed by accepting parentheses; here all five pass with the calls bare. These are five runs, one Opus, so a move on one tier rests on one or two runs.

Other rules: Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call is listed for opus-1 (lines 109-111, a raise whose message is a string concatenation spread over two lines), to the standard of 2026-10-31 opus-1. Make polymorphism explicit is listed for haiku-2, the one run whose generated match/1 has no guard, to the standard of 2026-10-31-check-2 haiku-1. Smoke test outside the rules: all five return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", and return :error for "/nope"; opus-1 and sonnet-2 use string param keys, the other three atom keys. MyApp.Router.match(123) raises FunctionClauseError in the generated match/1 in the other four and in String.split/3 in haiku-2.
